Plan: CUDA GPU acceleration (issue #3)¶

Branch: 3-cuda-gpu, from main at 29dca41 (after the logging merge, PR #15). Status: steps 0–8 implemented (2026-10-19). The CPU-only build is tested on macOS. The CUDA build is compiled and tested in CUDA 12.6 and 12.8 containers with no GPU. The GPU code has not run on a GPU yet (see §9).

Earlier GPU work (wvt-gpu-dev, PR #5) is out of date. This plan starts again from main and does not use that branch.

1. Goal¶

Issue #3 asks for these items:

  1. Do the heavy DSP on an NVIDIA GPU when the computer has one. This reduces the time between the device and the display.

  2. Render images on the GPU where it is useful.

  3. Add CMake flags that turn the CUDA features on or off, based on the GPU or its drivers.

Hard rules:

  • The GPU result must look the same as the CPU result.

  • Every computer without a usable GPU must build, start and work exactly as main does now. This includes macOS, AMD or Intel graphics, and computers with no NVIDIA driver.

The FFT (src/dsp/dsp.cpp) is a scalar radix-2 FFT. The waterfall uses parallelFor over rows. Each FFT reads and decodes its own samples through IqFile::read. The file is memory-mapped.

Rendering today¶

  • The UI is ImGui + ImPlot with the OpenGL 2 backend over GLX. When GLX works, the GPU already draws the frame.

  • When GLX does not work, src/app/sw_renderer.cpp draws on the CPU. This happens with some XQuartz or remote X11 setups.

  • The waterfall image is at most 1024 × 2048. The CPU changes dB values to colors with a 256-entry lookup table (src/app/app.cpp, src/app/app_live.cpp), then sends the image with glTexImage2D.

That is a small part of the frame time. CUDA–OpenGL interop would need a direct GLX context on the NVIDIA driver. It cannot work over remote X11, which is a main use of wvt. Recommendation: no GPU work for rendering (see §8). Measure this first (step 0).

Build¶

  • CMakeLists.txt needs CMake 3.16. Optional parts use WVT_WITH_<X> = AUTO / ON / OFF (RTL-SDR, UHD, audio).

  • Self-test tools: siggen_check, audio_check and log_check.

  • The repository has no CI.

  • The development computer is a Mac. It has no CUDA.

3. Design decisions¶

Topic

Decision

Reason

Build switch

WVT_WITH_CUDA = AUTO / ON / OFF, default AUTO. AUTO builds the CUDA code when the CUDA toolkit is found. ON stops the build if the toolkit is not found.

Same pattern as the other optional parts.

“Based on presence of a GPU”

Build time: CMake checks for the CUDA toolkit (nvcc + cuFFT). Run time: wvt checks for the GPU and the driver.

The computer that builds wvt is often not the one that runs it. A CUDA build must still run on a computer with no GPU.

CMake details

include(CheckLanguage), check_language(CUDA), then enable_language(CUDA) and find_package(CUDAToolkit), all inside the CUDA block. The CUDA block needs CMake 3.18 or later; with an older CMake, skip it with a status line. On Apple, skip it, and stop the build if ON.

Non-CUDA builds do not change.

Code layout

src/gpu/gpu.h: plain C++ interface, no CUDA headers. src/gpu/gpu_cuda.cu: kernels + cuFFT. src/gpu/gpu_stub.cpp: build without CUDA, “not available”. src/gpu/gpu_common.cpp: code shared by both builds (option parsing, status text).

Callers stay plain C++. Same “one file per backend” style as sdr_*.cpp. The interface can later take a Vulkan or HIP backend.

FFT

cuFFT, single-precision C2C, batched plans

Fits “rows × avg” FFTs.

Data transfer

Copy raw samples (cu8, ci16, …) to the GPU through pinned buffers. Decode, window and FFT on the GPU. Copy back only rows × cols floats.

Two to eight times less PCIe traffic than decoded cf32. The output is small.

Geometry stays in C++

The engine still computes rows, hop, avg, cols, f0/f1, the spectrum and the percentiles. The GPU code replaces only the inner loop.

The two paths cannot drift apart on layout.

Concurrency

One CUDA context. Each user thread (the waterfall worker, the live spectrum thread) owns its own stream, buffers and plan cache.

cuFFT plans are not thread-safe to share. Streams let the live and file paths overlap.

Cancel

Process in chunks. Check cancelled() between chunks.

Keeps the “latest request wins” behavior of Worker (src/dsp/engine.h).

Fallback

Each GPU function returns false on any error. The caller then runs the CPU code for that request. After an error other than “out of memory”, that path stays on the CPU for the rest of the session.

Never lose a result because of the GPU.

Run-time switch

--gpu auto|on|off, --gpu-device N, env WVT_GPU. auto uses a device with compute capability 7.5 or later and at least 1 GB of free memory. on stops at startup, with the reason, if no GPU is usable.

Lets the user compare with the CPU, or avoid a driver problem.

Work budget

kMaxInputSamples and kMaxAnalyzeRate depend on the backend. The CPU keeps 256 M and 20 MS/s. The GPU values come from the benchmark (start at 2 G and 100 MS/s).

This is where the user sees the gain: wider views at 100 %, and full-rate live analysis.

Logging (#14)

Component gpu. The gpuInit result is INFO: device, compute capability, memory, CUDA and driver versions, or why the GPU is not used. Each fallback is WARN, one time for each path. Request times are DEBUG, through the existing Worker “job took” line plus the GPU kernel time.

Follows the logging rules in docs/design/verbose-logging-plan.md.

Match tolerance

Waterfall and spectrum: 0.05 dB on bins more than 20 dB above the noise floor. Channel filter I/Q: 1e-4 relative.

cuFFT and the radix-2 FFT round differently. Both are float.

4. Interface sketch (src/gpu/gpu.h)¶

#pragma once
// Optional NVIDIA GPU acceleration. In a build without CUDA every call reports
// "not available" and the caller uses its CPU code.
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include "iq_file.h"

enum class GpuMode : int { Auto = 0, On, Off };

struct GpuInfo {
    bool available = false;
    std::string name;    // "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (compute 8.9, 12.0 GB)"
    std::string reason;  // why not available: "built without CUDA", "no NVIDIA driver", ...
};

bool gpuInit(GpuMode mode, int device, std::string& err);  // once, from main()
const GpuInfo& gpuInfo();
bool gpuEnabled();            // available and not switched off
void gpuSetEnabled(bool on);  // UI switch

// File spectrogram: `rows` rows of `avg` FFTs of size n. FFT a of row r starts at
// sample llround(s0 + r*hop + (a+0.5)*hop/avg) - n/2 (zero outside the file).
// Writes rows*cols linear max-pooled powers (scaled by norm/avg) to lin.
struct GpuSpecReq {
    const IqFile* file; FormatParams fp;
    double s0, hop; int rows, avg, n, cols; const float* win; float norm;
};
bool gpuSpectrogram(const GpuSpecReq& r, float* lin, const std::function<bool()>& cancelled);

// Live spectrum: one per LiveEngine thread; owns its stream, buffers and plan.
class GpuLiveSpectrum {
public:
    static std::unique_ptr<GpuLiveSpectrum> create(int n, SampleFormat fmt);
    virtual ~GpuLiveSpectrum() = default;
    // raw: frames*n packed samples. pw: n fftshifted powers, summed over frames.
    virtual bool run(const uint8_t* raw, int frames, const float* win, float* pw) = 0;
};

5. Implementation steps¶

Each step builds and passes the tests on macOS (CPU only) before the next one. Each step is one commit.

  1. Baseline benchmark (no GPU code). Add tools/gpu_check.cpp:

    • It makes test signals with SigGen (tones, chirps, short pulses, noise) in each SampleFormat, and writes temp files.

    • It runs computeWaterfall, the live row math and computeDemod, and prints the times:

      • waterfall at N = 1024 / 8192 / 65536 and 1× / 10× / 100× zoom-out;

      • live rows at 20 / 40 / 61.44 MS/s;

      • channel filter with 255 / 2047 / 8191 taps.

    • It also measures the color lookup + texture upload time, to settle the rendering question.

    Record the CPU numbers on the Linux computer that has the GPU.

  2. Build switch and stub.

    • Add WVT_WITH_CUDA to CMakeLists.txt, with the CUDA block from §3 and the default CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES (§8).

    • Add gpu.h, gpu_stub.cpp and gpu_common.cpp, and a wvt_gpu library that both wvt and gpu_check link.

    • Status line: wvt: CUDA support enabled (CUDA 12.x, archs ..., cuFFT), or the reason it is disabled.

  3. Run-time setup.

    • gpuInit in gpu_cuda.cu. It treats cudaErrorNoDevice and cudaErrorInsufficientDriver as “not available”, and checks compute capability and free memory.

    • One CUDA_TRY macro that logs the first error (file and line) and returns false.

    • --gpu, --gpu-device and WVT_GPU in main.cpp, with usage text.

    • --list-devices also lists the GPUs.

  4. CI.

    • Add .github/workflows/build.yml with two jobs:

      • CPU-only Linux build that runs the self-tests;

      • build in an nvidia/cuda:12.x-devel-ubuntu24.04 container with -DWVT_WITH_CUDA=ON, compile only.

    • Without this step, nvcc errors show up only on the GPU computer. Free GitHub runners have no GPU, so gpu_check cannot run there.

  5. File waterfall on the GPU.

    • Split computeWaterfall into a geometry part and an inner loop. Call gpuSpectrogram when gpuEnabled(); otherwise run the existing parallelFor loop.

    • GPU side:

      • At 100 % coverage, copy the contiguous raw span in chunks of rows. Otherwise, gather only the FFT segments into the pinned buffer.

      • Kernel decodeWindow: same rules as decodeSamples (swapIQ, bigEndian, scale), times the window, zero outside the file.

      • Batched cufftExecC2C.

      • Kernel powerPool: |X|² summed over avg with fftshift, scaled, max-pooled to cols.

      • Two staging slots, so the copy of chunk k+1 overlaps the work on chunk k.

    • Raise the input budget on the GPU. gpu_check compares GPU and CPU results.

  6. Live spectrum on the GPU.

    • In spectrumLoop, make a GpuLiveSpectrum. Make it again when N or the format changes.

    • Send the raw slice that the loop already reads. Get back n powers. Column pooling stays in C++.

    • Make kMaxAnalyzeRate depend on the backend. Update the “up to 20 MS/s” tooltip in src/app/app_live.cpp.

    • Target: less than 2 ms of GPU time per row at 40 MS/s and 30 rows/s.

  7. UI.

    • Status bar tag GPU <name> or CPU. A tooltip with GpuInfo and the fallback notes.

    • A GPU checkbox in the view settings. It calls gpuSetEnabled and invalidates the workers, so the view computes again.

    • The live status bar shows (GPU) after “FFT sees”.

  8. Channel filter on the GPU (optional, after step 5 is measured).

    • Move the NCO + FIR + decimate of dense processRange to the GPU. Keep the NCO phase from the absolute sample index in double precision.

    • Use a direct polyphase kernel for a small number of taps, and overlap-save FFT convolution for many taps.

    • The atan2 / unwrap / smoothing stays on the CPU.

    • Do this step only if step 0 shows that the channel filter is slow. It can also go to a new issue.

  9. README.

    • Add the section “Optional: GPU acceleration”: requirements, WVT_WITH_CUDA, CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES, --gpu, and how to check with --list-devices.

    • Add the new files to the file table.

6. Testing¶

Where

What

macOS (each step)

Build with no warnings. siggen_check, audio_check, log_check and gpu_check (CPU only) pass. Output and log with no --gpu flag match main, except the new INFO line. --gpu on stops with the reason.

CI (step 3 on)

The CPU-only job and the CUDA compile job pass.

Linux + NVIDIA GPU (steps 4–7, you must do this)

Build with -DWVT_WITH_CUDA=ON. gpu_check passes the tolerances in §3. Record the gpu_check --bench times. Run the GUI with a file and with --device sim: GPU checkbox, status bar, and a forced error to check the fallback.

Linux, CUDA build, no GPU or driver

wvt starts, shows CPU, works, and the log gives the reason.

7. Acceptance criteria¶

  1. A build with WVT_WITH_CUDA=OFF, and every macOS build, has no change in behavior.

  2. A CUDA build on a computer without an NVIDIA driver starts and works on the CPU.

  3. gpu_check passes on at least one RTX card.

  4. File waterfall: at least 5× faster than the CPU at N = 8192 and 100× zoom-out. 100 % coverage for a view at least 4× wider than the CPU budget allows.

  5. Live: at 40 MS/s with auto averaging, “FFT sees” stays at 100 % at 30 rows/s. The spectrum thread causes no dropped samples.

  6. A forced CUDA error moves that path to the CPU, logs a WARN, and the view still updates.

8. Decisions needed¶

  1. GPU rendering. Recommendation: leave it out (§2). OpenGL already draws on the GPU, and CUDA–GL interop fails over remote X11. Step 0 measures it. Do you agree?

  2. Target hardware. Desktop GeForce RTX (sm_75 / 86 / 89 / 120), data-center cards (sm_80 / 90), or Jetson (aarch64)? This sets CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES and the build time.

  3. Linking. Static cuFFT gives a binary of about 100–200 MB that needs only the driver. Shared cuFFT gives a small binary that needs the CUDA toolkit libraries at run time. Recommendation: static, because it runs with only the driver. The CPU build does not change.

  4. Minimum CUDA version. Recommendation: 12.0, with 12.8 or later recommended (needed for RTX 50 / sm_120).

  5. CI. Can step 3 add GitHub Actions to the repository?

  6. Test computer. Is there a Linux computer with an NVIDIA GPU for steps 4–7, and which card?

  7. Scope for closing #3. Close #3 after steps 0–6 and 8, and move the channel filter (step 7) to a new issue?

9. Implementation notes¶

The decisions in §8 are still open. Until they are answered, the code uses the recommendations: static cuFFT, CUDA 12.0 or later, and desktop RTX + data-center targets.

Differences from the plan¶

  • gpuInit runs only on the GUI path. The headless paths (--audio-out, --no-gui, --gen-out, --tx) do not use the waterfall, so they do not start CUDA, and their output is the same as main.

  • gpu_check makes its own test signal (two tones, a chirp, 1 µs pulses, noise) as one ci16 file. It does not use SigGen. The other formats come with the GPU decode checks in step 4.

  • --gpu off never calls the CUDA driver.

  • Default CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES: 75-real 80-real 86-real 89-real 90 (PTX for newer GPUs), plus 120 with CUDA 12.8 or later. A value given on the command line wins.

Step 4: file waterfall on the GPU¶

File

Change

src/gpu/gpu.h

SpecJob (the plan’s GpuSpecReq, shared by the CPU and the GPU), specFftStart, GpuStatus (Ok, Cancelled, Unavailable, Failed), gpuSpectrogram, gpuSpectrogramUsable.

src/gpu/gpu_common.cpp

The fallback rules: after a failure other than “out of memory”, the waterfall stays on the CPU until the next gpuInit; one WARN. Out of memory: WARN once, the path stays on. WVT_GPU_FORCE_FAIL=1 forces a failure.

src/gpu/gpu_cuda.cu

gpuBackendSpectrogram, below. CUDA_TRY / CUFFT_TRY now return Failed with the message instead of logging.

src/dsp/engine.h, src/dsp/engine.cpp

computeWaterfall keeps the geometry and tries the GPU first (budget 2 G samples); on any result other than Ok or Cancelled it computes avg again with the CPU budget and runs spectrogramCpu, the old loop moved out unchanged. WaterfallRes::gpu says which one ran.

src/io/iq_file.h

IqFile::data(): the mapped bytes, for the upload.

CMakeLists.txt

CUDA C++20 (the headers use defaulted operator==). Static cuFFT needs CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION and CUDA_RESOLVE_DEVICE_SYMBOLS on wvt_gpu (device link). segment_check links wvt_gpu.

tools/gpu_check.cpp

GPU against CPU in all 6 formats, big-endian, swapped I/Q, a 3-byte header, FFTs before and after the file, rows longer than one chunk, computeWaterfall, cancel, and the forced failure. --bench adds GPU columns.

How the GPU path works:

  • The work goes in chunks of up to 8 M samples (kChunkSamples). A chunk holds whole rows, or, when one row needs more, part of one row; the row sums go on in a device buffer.

  • The CPU threads copy the raw bytes of each FFT from the mapped file into one of two pinned buffers. The copy of chunk k+1 runs while the GPU works on chunk k (a CUDA event per buffer). The plan’s “contiguous span at 100 % coverage” shortcut is not done: each FFT is copied on its own, so 50 % overlap copies each sample twice. Measure first.

  • Kernels: decodeWindowKernel (the decodeSamples rules, the window, zero outside the file), batched in-place cufftExecC2C, accumulateKernel (|X|² with fftshift, summed per row, no atomics), poolKernel (scale and max over the bins of each column).

  • Each thread has its own stream, buffers and up to 4 cached cuFFT plans. The batch is a power of two, so few plans are made. The buffers stay allocated between calls.

  • Cancel is checked before each chunk.

Checks:

  • macOS: the CPU waterfall is bit-identical to before the change (checksums of 24 waterfalls: 6 formats × 4 views, compared with a build from before the split). All self-tests pass, with no warnings.

  • CUDA 12.8 container, static cuFFT: builds with no warnings, the self-tests pass, and gpu_check skips the comparison (“no NVIDIA driver”).

  • CUDA 12.6 container, -DWVT_CUDA_STATIC=OFF: the same; wvt loads libcudart.so.12 and libcufft.so.11.

  • Binary size: 272 MB with static cuFFT and the 6 default GPU targets, 4.7 MB with shared cuFFT. This is more than the 100–200 MB in §8 item 3. Fewer targets (-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89) make it smaller.

Still to do on the GPU computer: gpu_check (the comparisons above must pass at 0.05 dB) and gpu_check --bench --samples 1G. Then set the GPU budget (2 G samples now) from the times. The budget is wall time, not only FFT work: a wide view reads up to 8× more of the file than on the CPU.

Step 5: live spectrum on the GPU¶

File

Change

src/gpu/gpu.h

GpuLiveSpectrum (a class with a hidden backend object, not the virtual create of §4, so the fallback rules stay in gpu_common.cpp) and gpuLiveUsable. run takes the format, N and the frame count on each call, so the loop does not make a new object when N or the format changes.

src/gpu/gpu_common.cpp

The fallback rules are now per path (PathState): a live failure turns off only the live path, and a waterfall failure only the waterfall. gpuInit resets both.

src/gpu/gpu_cuda.cu

gpuBackendLiveRun: copy the raw row up, then decodeWindowKernel (no “inside the file” table), batched cuFFT, and accumulateKernel as one row of all the frames. Rows over 8 M samples go in chunks. The plan cache is shared (PlanCache).

src/device/live.cpp

spectrumLoop tries the GPU first. Auto averaging analyzes up to 100 MS/s on the GPU (kGpuMaxAnalyzeRate) and 20 MS/s on the CPU. The column pooling and the “FFT sees” figure are unchanged. On a GPU failure the CPU does that row; the next rows use the CPU cap.

src/device/live.h

Stats::gpu: the last row came from the GPU (for the status bar in step 6).

src/app/app_live.cpp

The Avg tooltip: “up to 20 MS/s, or 100 MS/s on the GPU”.

tools/gpu_check.cpp

GPU against CPU for cu8, ci16 at 20 and 61.44 MS/s, one frame, big-endian cf32 with swapped I/Q, and N 65536 over two chunks. A forced live failure turns off only the live path. --bench adds the GPU time per row.

The row is copied from ordinary (pageable) memory: at 100 MS/s and 30 rows/s that is 13 MB per row for ci16. If the benchmark shows the copy matters, read the ring straight into a pinned buffer.

Checks: macOS (no warnings, all self-tests pass, --device sim records with the live loop running) and the CUDA 12.8 container (no warnings, self-tests pass, comparisons skipped: “no NVIDIA driver”).

Still to do on the GPU computer: gpu_check and gpu_check --bench; then the GUI with a USRP at 40 MS/s or more (acceptance §7 item 5: “FFT sees” stays at 100 % at 30 rows/s, no dropped samples).

Differences from the plan:

  • Builds without CUDA show nothing new: no tag, no checkbox. This keeps the “macOS builds do not change” rule (§1). A CUDA build always shows the tag: CPU when no GPU can be used, with the reason in the tooltip. The checkbox appears only when a GPU can be used.

  • The tag uses the short model name (“GPU GeForce RTX 4070”); the full name is in the tooltip.

Checks:

  • macOS: no warnings, the self-tests pass. The X display could not be opened from this session, so the Mac GUI was not looked at; by the code, a build without CUDA draws the same status bar as before.

  • CUDA 12.8 container with Xvfb and --software, no driver: the screenshots show CPU | software | 39 fps (file) and FFT sees 99% | CPU | software | 56 fps (live --device sim). No GPU checkbox, as expected.

Still to do on the GPU computer: the tag shows GPU <model>; turning the checkbox off and on computes the view again on the other side (the log has “GPU processing off / on”); the live status shows (GPU); with WVT_GPU_FORCE_FAIL=1 the tag shows CPU and its tooltip has the fallback note.

Step 8: README¶

“Optional: GPU acceleration” after “Optional: device support” (requirements, the CMake options, --gpu, the checkbox, the fallback, gpu_check). The options list, the live Avg text (100 MS/s on the GPU), the waterfall budget (2 G on the GPU), the status bar row and the source table are updated.

Step 7: channel filter on the GPU¶

Done after step 6, without a GPU measurement first: the CPU baseline already shows the filter as the slowest job (660 ms for 8191 taps on 8 MS).

File

Change

src/gpu/gpu.h

ChanJob (mix, FIR, decimate; shared by the CPU and the GPU), gpuChannelize, gpuChannelUsable.

src/gpu/gpu_common.cpp

A third fallback path, “channel filter”.

src/gpu/gpu_cuda.cu

decodeOne (the decode rules, now shared by all kernels), decodeMixKernel (decode, zero outside the file, mix with the phase from the absolute index: frac * index in double, reduced to [0, 1), then sincospif in float), firKernel (direct FIR, only the kept outputs, taps in shared memory up to 12000), gpuBackendChannelize (chunks of up to 8 M input samples; the raw bytes go up straight from the mapping).

src/dsp/engine.h, src/dsp/engine.cpp

channelizeCpu: the old mix + FIR code, moved unchanged. processRange tries the GPU in dense mode when the job has at least 2·10⁷ multiply-adds (kGpuMinChanMacs, a few ms of CPU work); sparse mode (short blocks per pixel) stays on the CPU. The atan2 / unwrap / smoothing stays on the CPU.

tools/gpu_check.cpp

GPU against CPU (1e-4 of the peak): 255 to 13001 taps, decimation 1 to 10, no mix, before and after the file, 3 chunks, cu8 / ci16 / cf32; cancel; a forced failure turns off only this path. --bench adds the GPU column.

Differences from the plan: no overlap-save FFT convolution for many taps. The direct kernel does N multiply-adds per kept output with the taps in shared memory; the benchmark on the GPU will show if FFT convolution is needed.

Checks: the CPU demodulator is bit-identical to before (checksums of 18 computeDemod results: cf32 / ci16 / cu8, dense and sparse, decimation 1, 8191 taps, mix on and off, views before and past the file). macOS and the CUDA 12.8 container: no warnings, all self-tests pass, the GPU comparisons are skipped there.

Still to do on the GPU computer: gpu_check and the channel filter rows of gpu_check --bench.

Step 3: CI¶

.github/workflows/build.yml, on pushes to main and on pull requests, or by hand (a newer push to the same branch cancels the running one). Pushes to other branches build only through their pull request, so each commit builds once. actions/checkout@v5 (Node.js 24).

Job

What it does

Linux (CPU, RTL-SDR, UHD)

Ubuntu 24.04 with librtlsdr-dev and libuhd-dev, WVT_WITH_CUDA=OFF. Builds, runs the 5 self-tests, --list-devices, and a headless WAV export with --segment.

Linux CUDA 12.0 (compile only)

nvidia/cuda:12.0.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 (CMake 3.22): the minimum CUDA version.

Linux CUDA 12.8 (compile only)

nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu24.04: adds sm_120.

The CUDA jobs build with -DWVT_WITH_CUDA=ON and run the self-tests with no GPU, so they also check the “CUDA build on a computer without a GPU” rule; --gpu on must fail.

Found while adding it: CMake before 3.25 does not know nvcc’s C++20 flag, so the CUDA 12.0 build on Ubuntu 22.04 failed to configure. CMakeLists.txt now defines CMAKE_CUDA20_STANDARD_COMPILE_OPTION when CMake lacks it.

Checked before pushing: the CPU job’s steps in an ubuntu:24.04 container (RTL-SDR and UHD on, no warnings, all pass), and both CUDA images (no warnings, all pass). The containers were arm64; the GitHub runners are x86-64.
